The patient's bitemporal hemianopsia and the presence of a sellar/suprasellar mass are also consistent with a granular cell tumor, a type of tumor that can compress the optic chiasm.
The patient's bitemporal hemianopsia and the presence of a sellar/suprasellar mass are also consistent with a chordoma, a type of tumor that can compress the optic chiasm.
The patient's bitemporal hemianopsia and the presence of a sellar/suprasellar mass are also consistent with a glioma, a type of tumor that can compress the optic chiasm.
